original_test_intent: Read complete information for one approved BMC channel and validate its medium, protocol, session support and OEM identifier against the product recipe without mutation.
original_method: Retain raw 0x06/0x42 and source OEM-byte checkpoint; make the hard-coded value conditional on authoritative SKU evidence.
manual_activity: Owner confirms channel mapping and whether F2 1B 00 is authoritative for this product/SKU.
safety_requirements: Do not assume F2 1B 00 across every SKU
agent_execution_scope: Compare OEM bytes with approved recipe
Preserve raw/redacted evidence and non-mutation proof

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Not fit: the standard command is already explicit; the missing product oracle does not make execution mechanics undefined.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use one protected `ipmitool ... raw 0x06 0x42 <approved-channel>` and parse the complete response before applying the approved OEM-ID comparison.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Opcode, channel placeholder, OEM checkpoint and 10/5 timing remain preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Decode the full standard response and apply a SKU-bound vendor-ID oracle.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds target/recipe binding and complete field validation while removing log clearing.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Checking only bytes 6-8 misses malformed or contradictory medium/protocol/session fields.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A universal hard-coded OEM value can falsely fail another legitimate SKU or conceal a wrong target.

project_override_considerations: A vendor inventory API can corroborate the identifier but replaces raw coverage only when field mapping and channel identity are documented.
expected_evidence: Recipe OEM value and byte-position comparison

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Master explicitly provides raw 0x06/0x42 while DeepSeek says exact bytes are unavailable; the Master also hard-codes an OEM ID without visible SKU qualification and asks to clear logs.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The read is standard. Channel and SKU-specific expected vendor ID are execution-readiness inputs.

review_improvement: Retains the OEM checkpoint but makes it product-authoritative and verifies the complete channel response rather than a successful exit plus three bytes.
independent_technical_reasoning: OEM identifier bytes are meaningful only after completion, response length and surrounding field layout establish the correct response schema. Binding the expected ID to the actual product recipe prevents a copied Wistron value from being treated as universal and helps distinguish a true identity mismatch from querying the wrong BMC/channel.
